frs_sections.title: OVERVIEW
frs_sections.content:
===============================================================================

PROFINET is the open Industrial Ethernet standard for automation, standardized
in IEC 61158 (Type 10) and IEC 61784-2 (Communication Profile Family 3). It is
maintained by PI (PROFIBUS & PROFINET International). PROFINET runs on standard
100 Mbit/s and 1 Gbit/s switched Ethernet using standard IEEE 802.3 Ethernet
frames and standard Ethernet hardware (cables, connectors, PHYs, switches).

PROFINET is NOT a separate physical layer: it re-uses Fast Ethernet / Gigabit
Ethernet at the physical and MAC layers. What PROFINET adds is the
application-protocol layer for real-time cyclic process data exchange between
distributed field devices and controllers, the device model, the engineering
and address-assignment prot…

frs_sections.title: ETHERNET BASE LAYER
frs_sections.content:
===============================================================================

Physical / MAC base:
  - 100BASE-TX (Fast Ethernet) and 1000BASE-T (Gigabit Ethernet), full duplex,
    switched. Standard IEEE 802.3 framing: preamble, SFD, destination MAC,
    source MAC, EtherType/length, payload, FCS (CRC-32).
  - Standard 6-byte MAC addresses; standard Ethernet switching.
  - 100 Mbit/s is the baseline; PROFINET devices use auto-negotiation but
    typically run at fixed 100 Mbit/s full-duplex for deterministic behavior.

EtherType usage:
  - 0x8892  PROFINET Real-Time (RT/IRT) frames (also called the PNIO/PN-RT
            EtherType). Cyclic and acyclic real-time frames ride directly on
            Layer 2 with this EtherType, NOT inside IP.

frs_sections.title: DEVICE MODEL AND ROLES
frs_sections.content:
===============================================================================

PROFINET IO defines three device roles:

  - IO-Controller : typically a PLC (programmable logic controller). It runs
                    the automation program, establishes the Application
                    Relation(s) to the IO-Devices, sends cyclic output data
                    (provider) and consumes cyclic input data (consumer), and
                    handles alarms. There is one primary IO-Controller per AR
                    (a shared-device case may add further controllers).

  - IO-Device     : a distributed field device (remote I/O block, drive,
                    sensor/actuator station, valve terminal). It provides input
                    process data to and consumes output process data fr…

frs_sections.title: DIAGNOSIS AND ALARMS
frs_sections.content:
===============================================================================

PROFINET diagnosis is channel-, submodule-, and module-oriented:
  - Channel Diagnosis : a fault on a specific channel (e.g. wire break, short,
    over-temperature) with a ChannelErrorType code, ChannelNumber, and
    severity (maintenance required / maintenance demanded / fault).
  - Alarms (sent on the Alarm-CR, EtherType 0x8892):
      Diagnosis Alarm (appearing / disappearing),
      Process Alarm,
      Plug / Pull Alarm (a module was inserted/removed in a slot),
      Return-of-Submodule Alarm,
      Status / Update Alarm.
    Alarms have a low and a high priority queue and an explicit acknowledge.
  - The Data Status bit "Station Problem Indicator" gives the controller a
    quick station-level health …

frs_sections.title: SECURITY
frs_sections.content:
===============================================================================

Classic PROFINET IO has no built-in cryptographic protection of the cyclic
real-time path; security relies on network segmentation, the security classes
of the automation cell, and defense-in-depth (firewalls, zones/conduits per
IEC 62443). The integrity of cyclic frames against transmission errors is
provided by the Ethernet FCS (CRC-32) plus the APDU Cycle Counter / Data Status
and the IOPS/IOCS per-object validity. PROFINET Security (a later PI
specification layer) adds authentication and integrity for the engineering and
acyclic channels; it is layered above the classic IO data path and is out of
scope for the base cyclic protocol described here.

frs_sections.title: VERSIONING
frs_sections.content:
===============================================================================

PROFINET is standardized in IEC 61158 (Type 10 — PROFINET IO services, protocol
and application layer) and IEC 61784-2 (CPF 3, the communication profiles
RT_CLASS_1 / RT_CLASS_2 / RT_CLASS_3(IRT) / RT_CLASS_UDP). It is maintained by
PI (PROFIBUS & PROFINET International). The performance classes (NRT, RT, IRT),
the conformance classes (CC-A, CC-B, CC-C), the GSDML device-description schema,
the DCP addressing protocol, the AR/CR connection model, the cyclic PNIO data
with IOPS/IOCS and APDU status, the acyclic CL-RPC records, the PTCP time
synchronization, and the MRP media redundancy together define the PROFINET IO
communication standard.

PROFINET deliberately distinguishes itself from its serial predecessor…

protocol_overview.type: Industrial Ethernet application protocol on standard switched IEEE 802.3 (100 Mbit/s / 1 Gbit/s). Cyclic provider/consumer process data (PNIO) plus acyclic record services, with three performance classes NRT / RT / IRT and a device model of IO-Controller / IO-Device / IO-Supervisor.
protocol_overview.duplex: full-duplex switched Ethernet; cyclic data uses a provider/consumer model (the IO-Device provides inputs and consumes outputs, the IO-Controller the reverse), not request/response.
protocol_overview.encoding: PHY-class specific: 100BASE-TX uses 4B/5B then MLT-3; 100BASE-FX uses 4B/5B then NRZI; 1000BASE-T uses PAM5 with 8B1Q4 + Trellis coding; 1000BASE-X uses 8B/10B (same code as Fibre Channel / PCIe 1.x); 10BASE-T uses Manchester. MII/GMII/RGMII themselves carry plain LVTTL/LVCMOS nibble or byte data — encoding happens entirely inside the PHY.
interfaces_in_scope: Clause 4 — MAC frame format + CSMA/CD + full-duplex operation
Clause 22 — Reconciliation Sublayer (RS) + MII (10/100 Mb/s) + MDC/MDIO + Clause-22 management registers
Clause 45 — MMD-extended MDIO management (5-bit MMD + 16-bit register address per PHY)
Clause 28 — Auto-Negotiation (out-of-band Fast Link Pulse / Base Page exchange)
Clause 31 — MAC Control sublayer (PAUSE frame mechanism for full-duplex flow control)

frame_classes.Data_frame: Preamble + SFD + DA + SA + EtherType/Length + Payload + Pad + FCS
frame_classes.VLAN_tagged_frame: Preamble + SFD + DA + SA + VLAN tag (TPID 0x8100 + TCI) + EtherType/Length + Payload + Pad + FCS (max 1522 B)
frame_classes.PAUSE_frame: DA = 01:80:C2:00:00:01 (Slow Protocols Multicast) + SA + EtherType 0x8808 + Opcode 0x0001 + Pause Quanta (16b) + zero pad to 64 B + FCS
frame_classes.MDIO_C22_frame: PRE(32) + ST(01) + OP(read=10/write=01) + PHYAD(5) + REGAD(5) + TA(2) + DATA(16)
frame_classes.MDIO_C45_frame: PRE(32) + ST(00) + OP(addr=00/write=01/read=11/postRead=10) + PRTAD(5) + DEVAD(5) + TA(2) + DATA(16) — two-cycle protocol: address then read/write
frame_classes.Auto-Negotiation: 16-bit Base Page (Clause 28.2.1) advertised via Fast Link Pulse (FLP) bursts; encodes Selector / Tech Ability / Acknowledge / Remote Fault / Next Page

protocol_overview.base_layer: Standard IEEE 802.3 Fast/Gigabit Ethernet — standard frames (preamble, SFD, MAC addresses, EtherType, payload, FCS/CRC-32), standard switching; PROFINET is NOT a separate PHY/MAC.

performance_classes.name: RT
performance_classes.transport: Layer-2 Ethernet, EtherType 0x8892, VLAN PCP priority 6

protocol_overview.vlan_priority: IEEE 802.1Q VLAN tag; RT cyclic uses PCP = 6
protocol_overview.device_model: Slot / Subslot structure; Device Access Point (DAP) = slot 0; Module Ident Number / Submodule Ident Number matched to the expected engineering configuration.
protocol_overview.addressing: Name-based: NameOfStation assigned via DCP (Discovery and Configuration Protocol); IP (address/mask/gateway) also via DCP (DHCP optional); LLDP for topology/neighbor detection.
protocol_overview.connection_model: Application Relation (AR) established via CL-RPC Connect; carries IO-CR (cyclic), Record-Data-CR (acyclic Read/Write), Alarm-CR.
protocol_overview.cyclic_data: PNIO: each submodule's IO data object travels with a 1-byte IOPS (provider status, Good/Bad) and the reverse frame carries IOCS (consumer status); the frame appends an APDU Status (2-byte Cycle Counter, Data Status, Transfer Status).
protocol_overview.acyclic_data: CL-RPC (connectionless DCE/RPC over UDP): Connect/Release, Read/Write records (parameters, diagnosis, I&M0..I&M4), Control (ParameterEnd/ApplicationReady).
protocol_overview.time_sync: PTCP (Precision Transparent Clock Protocol), sync domain

compliance_requirements: Standard IEEE 802.3 switched Ethernet base (100 Mbit/s / 1 Gbit/s, full duplex).
DCP name/IP assignment and (CC-B+) LLDP topology / SNMP diagnosis.
GSDML device description matching the real device.
AR establishment via CL-RPC with IO-CR / Record-Data-CR / Alarm-CR.
Cyclic provider/consumer data with per-object IOPS/IOCS and APDU Cycle Counter / Data Status.
RT cyclic frames on EtherType 0x8892 with VLAN PCP prioritization.
Declared conformance class behavior (CC-A / CC-B / CC-C); CC-C adds IRT scheduling and PTCP sync.

functional_requirements.text: PROFINET runs on standard switched IEEE 802.3 Fast/Gigabit Ethernet using standard frames and hardware; it adds an application protocol and does NOT define a new PHY/MAC.
Three performance classes coexist: NRT (TCP/IP, UDP), RT (Layer-2 EtherType 0x8892, VLAN PCP priority), and IRT (hardware-scheduled isochronous real-time in a sync domain).
Devices take one of three roles: IO-Controller (PLC), IO-Device (field device), IO-Supervisor (engineering/diagnostics).
Each IO-Device is described by a GSDML XML file (VendorID/DeviceID, modules/submodules, I/O sizes, parameters, supported features) imported by the engineering tool.
Stations are addressed by NameOfStation via DCP (Identify/Get/Set/Hello); DCP also assigns the IP configuration (DHCP optional); LLDP provides topology/neighbor detection.
The IO-Controller establishes an Application Relation (AR) to an IO-Device via CL-RPC Connect, carrying the expected configuration.
An AR contains Communication Relations: one or more IO-CR (cyclic), a Record-Data-CR (acyclic Read/Write), and an Alarm-CR (alarms).
An IO-Device is organized in slots/subslots; the Device Access Point is slot 0; Module/Submodule Ident Numbers must match the expected configuration or diagnosis is raised.
Cyclic IO-CR data carries each data object with its provider status IOPS (Good/Bad); the reverse frame carries the consumer status IOCS; partial validity is signalled per submodule.

Each cyclic frame appends an APDU Status: a 2-byte Cycle Counter (31.25 us ticks), a Data Status byte (DataValid, Provider State, Station Problem Indicator, Primary/Backup), and a Transfer Status byte.

The cyclic timing is send_clock = 31.25 us x send-clock-factor; each CR has a reduction ratio, phase, and watchdog (data-hold = reduction x send_clock x watchdog_factor); a watchdog miss flags the data invalid.
Acyclic services use CL-RPC (DCE/RPC over UDP): Connect/Release, Read/Write records by (API, Slot, Subslot, Index), Control (ParameterEnd/ApplicationReady), and the I&M0..I&M4 identification records.
Conformance Classes define interoperable feature sets: CC-A (RT), CC-B (CC-A + topology/diagnosis via SNMP/LLDP + MRP), CC-C (CC-B + IRT hardware).
IRT devices synchronize their clocks via PTCP within a sync domain (Sync Master + Sync Slaves; delay-request/response; sub-microsecond accuracy).
MRP provides Ethernet ring redundancy with one Media Redundancy Manager blocking a port and <= 200 ms recovery (part of CC-B and above).

error_response_conditions: Watchdog (data-hold) timeout — no valid cyclic frame within reduction x send_clock x watchdog_factor; consumer flags IOPS BAD / data invalid and the AR may abort.
Configuration mismatch — plugged Module/Submodule Ident Number does not match the expected configuration; Connect or diagnosis flags it.
AR abort — CL-RPC abort or fatal diagnosis tears down the AR; cyclic exchange stops and the device re-addresses/re-connects.
DCP name/IP not set — device has no NameOfStation; the IO-Controller cannot resolve and connect it.
Alarm — diagnosis/process/plug-pull alarms on the Alarm-CR with acknowledge; Station Problem Indicator set in the cyclic Data Status.
Ethernet FCS/CRC error — the standard Ethernet frame check discards corrupted frames (treated as a missed cyclic frame by the consumer).
